title: What Really Happened in the Stanford Prison Experiment?
subtitle: 史丹佛監獄實驗到底發生了什麼？一個經典研究的重新檢視
source: 原創議題文章；依 Wikipedia〈Stanford prison experiment〉（含 Le Texier 2019、Banuazizi & Movahedi 1975、Carnahan & McFarland 2007、Haslam & Reicher BBC Prison Study 之整理），2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Le Texier, T. (2019). Debunking the Stanford Prison Experiment. American Psychologist, 74(7), 823–839.

beginner.title: Guards and Prisoners
paras: In August 1971, a professor called Philip Zimbardo built a pretend prison in the basement of a building at Stanford University in the United States. He paid 24 male college students $15 a day. Some students became “guards” and others became “prisoners”. The pretend prison was in Jordan Hall, the university’s psychology building. Real police officers even “arrested” the prisoners at the start.
1971 年 8 月，一位名叫菲利普．津巴多的教授，在美國史丹佛大學一棟大樓的地下室裡，搭建了一座假監獄。他付錢給 24 名男大學生，每天 15 美元。有些學生扮演「獄警」，有些扮演「囚犯」。這座假監獄位於大學的心理學大樓喬丹館。實驗一開始，還有真正的警察來「逮捕」這些囚犯。

The study was planned to last two weeks. But very quickly, some guards began to treat the prisoners badly. They shouted at them and made them do push-ups. One prisoner seemed to have a breakdown after just 36 hours. A visiting psychologist was shocked by what she saw. Zimbardo stopped the study after only six days.
這項研究原本計畫進行兩週。但很快地，有些獄警開始虐待囚犯，對他們大吼，還要他們做伏地挺身。一名囚犯在短短 36 小時後似乎精神崩潰了。一位來訪的心理學家對眼前所見感到震驚。津巴多只進行了六天就停止了研究。

For many years, people used this study to teach one lesson: put good people in a bad situation, and they will do bad things. The study appeared in many school textbooks and films. It seemed to show how powerful a situation can be.
很多年來，人們用這項研究來教一個道理：把好人放進壞的情境裡，他們就會做壞事。這項研究出現在許多教科書和電影裡，它似乎證明了情境的力量有多強大。

But later, people looked more closely. Recordings show that one of the researchers told a guard to be more “tough”. Many guards later said they were just acting. And in 2017, the prisoner who “broke down” said he had faked it so that he could leave and study for an exam.
但後來，人們更仔細地檢視。錄音顯示，其中一位研究人員曾叫一名獄警要更「兇」一點。許多獄警後來說他們只是在演戲。而在 2017 年，那位「崩潰」的囚犯說，他是裝的，這樣才能離開去準備考試。

So what does this famous study really tell us? Maybe it shows less about human nature and more about how easily people follow what they think others expect. It also teaches us something important: even famous studies need to be checked carefully.
那麼，這項著名的研究到底告訴了我們什麼？也許它揭示的，與其說是人性，不如說是人們多麼容易照著自己認為別人期望的方式去做。它也教了我們一件重要的事：即使是有名的研究，也需要仔細檢驗。

intermediate.title: What Really Happened in the Stanford Prison Experiment?
paras: In August 1971, Stanford psychology professor Philip Zimbardo turned a university basement into a mock prison. A newspaper advertisement offered male college students $15 a day to take part in a “psychological study of prison life”. Twenty-four were selected after tests of psychological stability and randomly assigned to be guards or prisoners. The study was planned to last two weeks. To make it feel real, the “prisoners” were arrested at the start by real police officers from Palo Alto.
1971 年 8 月，史丹佛大學心理學教授菲利普．津巴多，把大學的地下室改造成一座模擬監獄。一則報紙廣告以每天 15 美元，招募男大學生參加一項「監獄生活心理研究」。經過心理穩定度測試後，有 24 人被選中，並被隨機分配擔任獄警或囚犯。研究原本預計進行兩週。為了讓一切感覺逼真，「囚犯」們在一開始是被帕羅奧圖的真正警察逮捕的。

Events escalated quickly. Guards made prisoners count off and do push-ups, restricted their use of the bathroom and forced them to use buckets in their cells. After 36 hours, prisoner 8612, Douglas Korpi, appeared to break down and was released. When the psychologist Christina Maslach visited and challenged Zimbardo about the conditions, he ended the experiment on the sixth day.
情況迅速升級。獄警要囚犯報數、做伏地挺身，限制他們上廁所，還強迫他們在牢房裡用水桶解決。36 小時後，8612 號囚犯道格拉斯．科爾皮似乎崩潰了，因而被釋放。心理學家克莉絲汀娜．馬斯拉赫來訪時，對這些情況提出質疑，津巴多於是在第六天結束了實驗。

For decades, the study was presented in textbooks as powerful evidence that situations can turn ordinary people cruel. Zimbardo himself compared the guards’ behaviour to the abuse of prisoners by American soldiers at Abu Ghraib. The message was simple and memorable: it is not bad people but bad situations that produce bad behaviour.
幾十年來，這項研究在教科書中被當成有力的證據，證明情境能讓普通人變得殘忍。津巴多本人也把獄警的行為，比作美軍在阿布格萊布監獄虐待囚犯的事件。這個訊息簡單又好記：造成惡行的不是壞人，而是壞的情境。

Critics, however, have raised serious doubts. Recordings released in 2017 show the “warden”, a research assistant, urging a guard to be tougher for the benefit of the experiment. Most guards later said they had been acting, and one said he had modelled his behaviour on a character from a film. In a 2017 interview, Korpi said his breakdown had been faked so he could leave and study for an exam, a claim Zimbardo disputed. The researcher Thibault Le Texier argued that Zimbardo had shaped the guards’ behaviour to confirm his expectations.
然而，批評者提出了嚴重的質疑。2017 年公開的錄音顯示，由研究助理擔任的「典獄長」，催促一名獄警為了實驗要更強硬。大多數獄警後來說他們是在演戲，其中一人說他是以電影裡的角色為範本。在 2017 年的一次訪談中，科爾皮說他的崩潰是裝出來的，好讓自己能離開去準備考試，但津巴多對此提出異議。研究者蒂博．勒泰西耶則主張，津巴多為了證實自己的預期，左右了獄警的行為。

Other studies point in a different direction. In the 2002 BBC Prison Study, guards were not told how to behave, and participants did not simply slip into cruel roles. The researchers concluded that leadership and group identity mattered more than the uniform. The Stanford experiment may therefore teach a different lesson from the one in many textbooks: even famous findings must be questioned, especially when they tell a story we find easy to believe.
其他研究指向不同的方向。在 2002 年的 BBC 監獄研究中，獄警並沒有被告知該怎麼做，參與者也沒有就這樣陷入殘忍的角色。研究人員的結論是：領導和群體認同比制服更重要。因此，史丹佛實驗教給我們的，可能和許多教科書不同：即使是著名的研究發現也必須被質疑，尤其當它講的是一個我們很容易相信的故事時。

advanced.title: A Classic Under Cross-Examination
paras: Few psychological studies have achieved the cultural reach of the Stanford prison experiment. Conducted in August 1971 and funded by the US Office of Naval Research, it was designed as a two-week simulation of prison life. Participants were recruited through a newspaper advertisement offering male college students $15 a day; twenty-four were selected after screening for psychological stability and assigned at random to the roles of guard or prisoner. Philip Zimbardo, the Stanford professor leading the project, cast himself as superintendent, while an undergraduate research assistant, David Jaffe, served as warden.
很少有心理學研究像史丹佛監獄實驗一樣，擁有如此廣泛的文化影響力。它於 1971 年 8 月進行，由美國海軍研究辦公室資助，原本設計為為期兩週的監獄生活模擬。參與者是透過一則報紙廣告招募的，廣告以每天 15 美元徵求男大學生；經過心理穩定度篩選後，選出二十四人，並隨機分配為獄警或囚犯。主持計畫的史丹佛教授菲利普．津巴多自任監獄主管，而大學部研究助理大衛．賈菲則擔任典獄長。

The study’s conventional narrative is dramatic. Guards subjected prisoners to arbitrary counts and push-ups, restricted their access to bathrooms and forced them to use buckets in their cells. After 36 hours, prisoner 8612, Douglas Korpi, appeared to suffer a breakdown and was released. When the psychologist Christina Maslach visited and confronted Zimbardo about the treatment of participants, he terminated the study on the sixth day, later saying he had been surprised by how deeply he had internalised his own role. The episode became a textbook illustration of the power of situations over individual character.
這項研究的傳統敘事十分戲劇化。獄警讓囚犯接受隨意的點名和伏地挺身，限制他們上廁所，並強迫他們在牢房裡使用水桶。36 小時後，8612 號囚犯道格拉斯．科爾皮似乎精神崩潰，因而被釋放。心理學家克莉絲汀娜．馬斯拉赫來訪時，就參與者受到的對待與津巴多當面對質，他在第六天終止了研究，後來表示自己很驚訝竟如此深入地內化了自己的角色。這段經過成為教科書中說明「情境凌駕個人性格」的經典例子。

That interpretation has faced sustained criticism. As early as 1975, Ali Banuazizi and Siamak Movahedi argued that participants were responding to demand characteristics — doing what they believed the researchers wanted — rather than to the prison environment itself. In 2007, Thomas Carnahan and Sam McFarland suggested that advertising a study of “prison life” may have attracted applicants already inclined towards aggression, a form of selection bias. Recordings that circulated widely in 2017 show the warden encouraging a reluctant guard to be “tough” for the sake of the experiment, and most guards have since said they were deliberately acting.

這種詮釋一直受到批評。早在 1975 年，阿里．巴努阿濟齊和西亞馬克．莫瓦赫迪就主張，參與者是在回應「需求特徵」——做他們認為研究者想要的事——而不是回應監獄環境本身。2007 年，湯瑪斯．卡納漢和山姆．麥克法蘭認為，以「監獄生活」為號召的廣告，可能吸引了原本就傾向攻擊性的應徵者，這是一種選擇偏誤。2017 年廣為流傳的錄音顯示，典獄長鼓勵一名不情願的獄警「為了實驗」要表現得「兇一點」，而大多數獄警事後也說他們是刻意在演戲。

The most pointed critique came in 2019, when Thibault Le Texier argued in American Psychologist that Zimbardo had instructed the guards to behave in certain ways in order to confirm conclusions largely formed in advance. Even the study’s most famous moment has been questioned: in a 2017 interview, Korpi claimed his breakdown had been faked so that he could leave and study for his graduate entrance exam. Zimbardo rejected these criticisms, maintaining that he had to treat the breakdown as genuine and that other guards behaved cruelly without any such encouragement.
最尖銳的批評出現在 2019 年：蒂博．勒泰西耶在《美國心理學家》期刊中主張，津巴多曾指示獄警以特定方式行事，以證實他大致早已形成的結論。就連研究中最著名的時刻也受到質疑：在 2017 年的一次訪談中，科爾皮聲稱他的崩潰是裝出來的，為的是能離開去準備研究所入學考試。津巴多駁斥這些批評，堅稱他必須把那次崩潰當真，而且其他獄警在沒有任何鼓勵的情況下也表現得很殘忍。

A partial replication offers a revealing contrast. In the 2002 BBC Prison Study, Alex Haslam and Steve Reicher gave guards no instructions on how to behave. Participants did not slip mindlessly into their roles, and the researchers concluded that tyranny emerged, when it did, through leadership and shared group identity rather than automatic conformity to a uniform. The lesson of the Stanford experiment may therefore be less about the darkness of human nature than about the fragility of scientific stories. A finding that is dramatic, memorable and morally satisfying deserves more scrutiny, not less.

一項部分重製的研究提供了鮮明的對照。在 2002 年的 BBC 監獄研究中，亞歷克斯．哈斯勒姆和史蒂夫．雷徹沒有告訴獄警該如何行事。參與者並沒有不假思索地陷入角色，研究者的結論是：暴政若真的出現，是透過領導與共享的群體認同，而不是自動服從於一身制服。因此，史丹佛實驗的教訓，與其說是關於人性的黑暗，不如說是關於科學故事的脆弱。一個戲劇化、令人難忘、又在道德上令人滿意的研究發現，值得更多的檢驗，而不是更少。

quote.text: Male college students needed for psychological study of prison life. $15 per day for 1–2 weeks beginning Aug 15.
quote.author: Recruitment advertisement for the Stanford prison experiment
quote.work: Palo Alto Times / The Stanford Daily, 1971, as shown in the Wikipedia article “Stanford prison experiment”

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How police officers train new prison guards.
How to build a real prison at a university.
Why college students enjoy doing push-ups for money.
A famous prison study and the doubts raised about it later.
beginner.evidence: It also teaches us something important: even famous studies need to be checked carefully.
beginner.why: 全文：史丹佛監獄實驗的經過、流傳的結論，以及後來的質疑。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：警察只是開場時「逮捕」囚犯。
字面誤讀：那是假監獄，只是實驗場景。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：伏地挺身是守衛對囚犯的懲罰。

beginner.q: What does “it” in “he had faked it” in the fourth paragraph refer to?
options: The guards’ push-ups.
The prisoner’s breakdown.
The prison’s basement.
The school textbook.
beginner.evidence: the prisoner who “broke down” said he had faked it
beginner.why: 同一句：崩潰的囚犯說他的崩潰是裝的。
traps: 張冠李戴：伏地挺身是守衛逼囚犯做的。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：地下室是監獄的地點。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：課本是傳播這個研究的地方。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The students were paid $50 a day.
The study lasted the full two weeks as planned.
Zimbardo stopped the study after only six days.
One guard had a breakdown after 36 hours.
beginner.evidence: Zimbardo stopped the study after only six days.
traps: 數字錯位：一天 15 美元。
正反顛倒：原本計畫兩週，六天就停了。
張冠李戴：崩潰的是囚犯。

beginner.q: What does the writer suggest the study may really show?
options: How easily people follow what they think others expect.
That all people become cruel in any prison.
That push-ups make students stronger.
That psychologists should never visit studies.
beginner.evidence: how easily people follow what they think others expect
traps: 以偏概全：作者正是質疑這個結論。
捏造：伏地挺身是懲罰，不是重點。
正反顛倒：來訪心理學家反而促成實驗停止。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: A famous study’s lesson has been seriously questioned.
Bad situations always turn good people cruel.
The BBC copied the Stanford study exactly in 2002.
Douglas Korpi designed the Stanford prison study.
intermediate.evidence: Critics, however, have raised serious doubts.
intermediate.why: 第四、五段：錄音、訪談與其他研究都質疑原本的結論。
traps: 以偏概全：這是被質疑的教科書說法。
正反顛倒：BBC 研究沒有指示守衛怎麼做，結果不同。
張冠李戴：Korpi 是囚犯 8612。

intermediate.q: What does “escalated” in the second paragraph most likely mean?
options: Ended earlier than planned.
Became calm and orderly.
Became more serious very quickly.
Moved to another building.
intermediate.why: 後面列出越來越嚴重的對待，可知是「迅速惡化」。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：提早結束是後來的結果。
正反顛倒：情況越來越糟。
捏造：實驗一直在地下室。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The guards and prisoners chose their own roles.
Real police officers arrested the “prisoners” at the start.
Zimbardo ended the study after Korpi complained.
Most guards said they had felt real hatred.
intermediate.evidence: the “prisoners” were arrested at the start by real police officers from Palo Alto
traps: 正反顛倒：角色是隨機分配的。
張冠李戴：是 Maslach 質疑後才停止。
正反顛倒：多數守衛說自己是在演戲。

intermediate.q: What did the 2002 BBC Prison Study suggest?
options: Prison studies cannot be repeated at all.
Guards always become cruel when given a uniform.
Prisoners should be paid more than guards.
Leadership and group identity mattered more than the uniform.
intermediate.evidence: The researchers concluded that leadership and group identity mattered more than the uniform.
traps: 正反顛倒：BBC 正是部分重做了這個研究。
正反顛倒：參與者沒有自動變殘忍。
捏造：文中沒提薪水比較。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To prove that human nature is mostly cruel.
To show why a famous study’s conclusion deserves more doubt.
To describe how the US Navy runs its prisons.
To praise Zimbardo for designing a perfect study.
advanced.evidence: A finding that is dramatic, memorable and morally satisfying deserves more scrutiny, not less.
traps: 正反顛倒：作者說重點不在人性黑暗。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：海軍研究辦公室只是出資者。
正反顛倒：研究方法受到嚴厲批評。

advanced.q: What are “demand characteristics” as described in the third paragraph?
options: Features of the prison building itself.
Prices that students demand for taking part.
Rules that guards demand prisoners obey.
Doing what participants believe the researchers want.
advanced.evidence: doing what they believed the researchers wanted
traps: 正反顛倒：原文說他們反應的不是監獄環境本身。
一字多義：demand 也有「要價」的意思，但這裡不是。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：守衛的規定是實驗內容，不是這個概念。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: David Jaffe, a research assistant, served as warden.
Zimbardo played the role of a prisoner.
Le Texier’s critique appeared in 1975.
Korpi said he wanted to leave to visit his family.
advanced.evidence: an undergraduate research assistant, David Jaffe, served as warden
traps: 張冠李戴：Zimbardo 擔任典獄長的上司（superintendent）。
時序錯置：Le Texier 是 2019 年，1975 年是另一篇批評。
捏造：他說是為了準備研究所考試。

advanced.q: Why might advertising a study of “prison life” cause selection bias?
options: It meant only women could take part.
It made students afraid to apply for the study.
It may have attracted people already inclined to be aggressive.
It told participants how to behave as guards.
advanced.evidence: may have attracted applicants already inclined towards aggression
traps: 正反顛倒：只招收男性大學生。
正反顛倒：問題是吸引了某類人，不是嚇跑人。
張冠李戴：告訴守衛要兇的是錄音中的典獄長。

reflections: Have you ever behaved differently because you thought someone expected you to? What happened?
Why do you think the original story of the Stanford experiment was so popular for so long?
